correctness_confidence.basis: All 18 Lean 4.35.0 theorems verified with zero sorry and zero Classical.choice, backed by exact rational arithmetic in Python DC-DELEG-CERT-1.0 and 60/60 adversarial forgery rejections.

novelty.basis: First complete machine-checked and exact-arithmetic verification framework for downward-closed combinatorial delegation bounds.

reproducibility.basis: Self-contained zero-dependency Lean module, deterministic exact-Q Python verifier, 16 canonical certificates, and SHA-256 artifact manifest enforcement.

rigor.basis: Meticulous formalization in Lean 4 and exact-Q rational arithmetic verifier covering combinatorial knapsack bounds, Bernstein positivity polynomials, and Taylor brackets.

significance.basis: Provides unbreakable formal and exact-rational guarantees for recent sharp combinatorial delegation bounds by Abdi et al.

strengths: 18 zero-sorry, zero-Classical.choice Lean 4.35.0 theorems covering core bounds, Efron-Stein variance, and Bernstein polynomials.
Exact-rational Python verifier DC-DELEG-CERT-1.0 using Python fractions with strict type and depth safety.
Comprehensive red-team audit with 60/60 live adversarial forgery rejections across global and domain-specific attack vectors.
Flawless reproducibility via tracked canonical certificates and SHA-256 artifact manifests.
strong_novelty_candidates: Zero-dependency Lean 4 formalization of downward-closed combinatorial delegation bounds
summary: The paper presents a rigorous formal verification and exact-rational certification framework (Lean 4.35.0 and DC-DELEG-CERT-1.0) for Abdi et al.'s improved downward-closed combinatorial delegation bounds. All 18 theorems are verified with zero sorry and zero Classical.choice, and 16 canonical certificates replay successfully while rejecting 60/60 adversarial forgeries.
weaknesses: Continuous integration proofs (like the 96-interval LP infeasibility solver and Lagrangian DP) are verified via exact certificate replay rather than full end-to-end continuous theorem proving in Lean.
